_: Golden for the uk.nopeak preset — D2 §9 1, D9 §3. The claim under test is that Great Britain bills households no capacity component at all.

sources.no_peak: HLD §8's UK/IE row: energy N2EX half-hourly, Agile and DFS events; grid TOU "none / Day-Night-Peak"; peak component `NoPeak` + reward events; hard limit the fuse. A domestic supply pays a standing charge per day and a unit rate per kWh — the DNO's capacity costs are inside the unit rate and are never measured against the household's own peak.
sources.window_min: 30 minutes, because that is the settlement period every British half-hourly tariff and every DFS event is quoted in; it costs nothing on a NoPeak preset and is right the moment a capacity component ever appears.
sources.metric_kw: 0.0 by construction on a NoPeak site; `level.metric_kw` is None.
sources.dfs: Demand Flexibility Service events are rewards on the price axis (D1), not a capacity metric, so they are deliberately absent here.
